claims.text: Deep cryogenic treatment can be used as a post-processing intervention for additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
Post-fabrication DCT will improve the dimensional precision of additively manufactured HEA components.
Post-fabrication DCT will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured HEA components.
Post-fabrication DCT will reduce fabrication-induced defects in additively manufactured HEA components.
DCT will relieve residual stresses in additively manufactured HEA components.
DCT will refine the microstructure of additively manufactured HEA components.
As-built additively manufactured HEA components exhibit residual stresses, microstructural inhomogeneities, and associated defects.
An effective DCT protocol should use temperatures near -196 degrees Celsius.
DCT should be performed immediately after additive manufacturing and followed by controlled warming.
DCT-mediated microstructural refinement includes decreased dislocation density.
Uniform cryogenic contraction redistributes and relieves internal stresses.
DCT promotes phase homogenization in the alloy.
DCT can induce a phase transition in an additively manufactured BCC HEA.
Stress relief and phase homogenization lead to fewer defects and improved dimensional stability.
DCT-treated additively manufactured HEA samples will have higher tensile strength than untreated as-deposited samples.
DCT-treated additively manufactured HEA samples will have greater ductility than untreated as-deposited samples.

The benefits of DCT will be most pronounced in AM HEAs with high residual stresses and microstructural inhomogeneities and less pronounced in processes already producing near-net-shape parts with few defects.
Optimal DCT temperature, soaking duration, and warming protocol vary with HEA composition and component geometry.
